title: Name on the Hummus
subject: a woman whose new flatmate writes his name on everything he puts in the shared fridge, so she starts labelling things back, until she sticks a label with her own name on his forehead and he laughs for the first time
caption: 70s Laurel Canyon soft-rock pop with a modern pop polish. Warm acoustic piano playing bouncy chords, a clean Telecaster with light chorus picking sunny fills, a round melodic bass, a dry 70s drum kit with tight snare, tambourine on the off-beats, a short flute fill between lines. Dry warm tape sound. Female soprano, breezy and deadpan, close stacked harmonies on the hook. 104 BPM, G major. Sly, sunny and petty. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM synths, no heavy distortion, no country twang.
lyrics:
[Intro - piano and flute]

[Verse 1]
New flatmate moved in Sunday
By Monday there were stickers
Kevin on the yoghurt
Kevin on the butter

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the cheese
Fine, Kevin
I bought stickers too, you'll see

[Verse 2]
Now the oven door says Becky
So do the ice tray and the bread
He wrote Kevin on the ketchup
I wrote Becky on his bed

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the keys
Name on the light switch
Name on the TV

[Bridge - just piano and tambourine]
Then I stuck one on his forehead
And he laughed out loud
First time I'd heard it

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the tea
Now the fridge door says
Kevin and me

[Outro - flute and Telecaster]
Fine, Kev, have the yoghurt
